name: Kinfolk
summary: Kinfolk is a London seed-stage startup (founded 2023, 1-10 employees per Crunchbase) selling AI agents that resolve employee HR requests inside Slack and Microsoft Teams, with a ticketing system behind them. The agents act, not just answer: they draft documents, update HRIS records and manage lifecycle changes, so they touch sensitive employee data in customer HRIS systems. It raised a $7.2M seed in Feb 2026 to scale enterprise readiness and expand into payroll and IT workflows.
product: AI-native HR/People Operations service-delivery platform: agentic AI ("Kin") in Slack/Teams, request ticketing and routing, lifecycle automation, analytics. Integrates with Workday, ADP, UKG, HiBob, BambooHR, Keka, Culture Amp, Google Drive, Confluence, SharePoint, Notion, OneDrive, Gmail, Outlook.

ai_usage.what: Customer-facing LLM agents answering employee HR requests in Slack/Teams and executing workflows (drafting documents, updating HRIS records, lifecycle changes) with approval gates, audit trail and cited answers. Verified in seed review: ships_customer_facing_llm=yes, agentic=true, confidence high.
surfaces: HRIS write actions (Workday, ADP, UKG, HiBob, BambooHR)

customers: Deliveroo (5,000 HR requests resolved in five months, 50% fewer Jira tickets)

headcount.current: 1-10 (Crunchbase range; likely understated, hiring GTM and engineering)
headcount.growth_note: Reported 5x YoY growth (Grishin Robotics, Mar 2026). Crunchbase seed total $7.2M; press reports $8.5M total raised to date.

news.title: Kinfolk closes $7M seed round for AI-driven HR platform (Tech.eu)
Kinfolk secures $7m seed to transform HR operations with agentic AI (AlbionVC)

compliance.soc2: SOC 2 Type II (self-reported, homepage and approach page)
compliance.eu_ai_act_exposure: High. Annex III treats AI used in employment and workers management (including task allocation, monitoring, decisions affecting work terms) as high-risk. Kinfolk is a provider and its customers are deployers; its agents handle employee requests and change HRIS records rather than screen candidates, so classification depends on use case, but customers will ask for human oversight, logging and risk controls.
compliance.notes: Also ISO 27001:2022, GDPR (DPA signed per customer), CCPA. Governance features exist already: roles, API scopes, approval gating, full audit trail, org-wide guardrails. London HQ, UK/EU customers. No public security incident found.

why_now: Kinfolk closed a $7.2M seed on 2026-02-25/26 (AlbionVC) explicitly to 'expand enterprise readiness' and extend agents into payroll and IT workflows, which widens write access to the most sensitive employee data; with Deliveroo live (5,000 requests in five months) and 5x YoY growth, enterprise security reviews and EU AI Act employment-AI scrutiny are arriving now while the team is still 1-10 people with no dedicated security or AI-safety hire visible.
likely_pains: Prompt injection through employee messages or ingested docs (Confluence, SharePoint, Notion) steering an agent that can write to HRIS
Data leaking across tenants or across departments inside a customer (salary, performance, medical leave, disciplinary cases) via retrieval or shared queues
Agents taking destructive or unauthorized actions (wrong record update, wrong employee, payroll change) beyond the approval gates
Employee-facing answers that are wrong or harmful on legal topics (leave, pay, dismissal), creating liability for the HR customer
Enterprise buyers demanding evidence of runtime guardrails and red-team results during security review
EU AI Act and UK/GDPR exposure from employment-related AI: logging, human oversight and automated decision rules

metrics.hypothesis: Time to pass enterprise security reviews, number of blocked/escalated risky agent actions, zero cross-tenant or PII incidents; supports Kinfolk's own 70% auto-resolution metric.

economic_buyer.hypothesis: CEO Jeet Mukerji at this size, possibly with CTO Kim Hellbom; budget is small and founder-controlled.

decision_criteria.hypothesis: Fast API integration (minutes), low latency in Slack/Teams flows, EU data region, SOC 2, policy flexibility per customer tenant, audit logs that map to Kinfolk's existing audit trail.

decision_process.hypothesis: Founder-led technical evaluation by CTO, trial on a staging agent, then sign; likely 2-4 weeks.

paper_process.hypothesis: Light: MSA/order form plus DPA; EU region matters for UK/EU customer base.

identify_pain.hypothesis: Enterprise prospects ask how agent actions are controlled and tested; founders have built approval gates in-house and may see runtime policy checks as undifferentiated work.

champion.hypothesis: CTO Kim Hellbom (ex-Beamery AI scaling) as technical champion.

competition.hypothesis: Build in-house (approval gating already exists), plus general guardrail vendors and model-provider filters; status quo of no runtime layer.

persona_angles.angle: Your agents already gate sensitive actions behind approvals; we add a runtime layer that checks every Slack message, retrieved doc and HRIS write against plain-language policies so you do not have to build and maintain that yourselves.
As you push into payroll and IT, every enterprise security review will ask how agent actions are controlled; we give you red-team results and live guardrails to hand them.
HR AI is high-risk under the EU AI Act, and we log which policy fired on each agent call so your customers get the oversight evidence they will ask for.

risks: Tiny team (1-10 employees) with limited budget and possible build-in-house preference
Already has SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and approval/audit controls, so the gap is narrower than at a typical AI startup
No security, AI-safety or CISO role identified; buyer is probably a founder
EU AI Act classification of its agents (employee support, not hiring decisions) is uncertain
Funding totals conflict across sources (7.2M vs 8.5M vs a mis-scraped 72M)
